summary: Shobha Rani Dash is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. Dash held a research post at Ryukoku University in 2010 and later posts at Otani University, attested as a lecturer in 2012 and professor in 2026.
Shodo Fujita is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University under Shoko Takeuchi. Between 1995 and 2013, he was attested as a guest researcher at Ryukoku University.
Shodo Yamagami is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Kyoto University from circa 1961 to 1964. He served as an assistant professor at Kyoto Sangyo University from around 1976 to 2010.

Shogo Watanabe, an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Toyo University and taught there from circa 1991 to 2024, becoming professor around 1996. He held posts at the Eastern Institute around 2024 and Taisho University around 2026.

Shohaku Okumura is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and under Kōshō Uchiyama. He founded Pioneer Valley Zendo and Sanshin Zen Community, taught at Minnesota Zen Meditation Center, and directed the Sōtō Zen Buddhism International Center (1997–2010).
Shoichi Ozawa was a Japanology and history and archaeology scholar who studied at Waseda University from circa 1948 to 1952. He later held a post at the Open University of Japan.

Shoji Mori is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned his BA and studied at Toyo University under Giyu Nishi. He taught at Toyo University from circa 1977 to 2009, and held a post at the Okura Institute.
Shoju Inaba was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a professor at Otani University from around 1949 to 1981 and held a part-time lecturer post at Nagoya University.

Shojun Bando was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1950 to 1954. He served at Ueno Gakuen University from around 1960 to 1998 and held a post at Otani University.

Shokin Furuta was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Tokyo University of Education under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki. He served as professor at Hokkaido University (~1951–1966) and Nihon University (~1966–1982).

Shoko Kanaoka was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who taught Stephan Marcus Salzberg. Kanaoka held posts at Toyo University, where an appointment as professor is attested in 1987 and a post is attested in 2000.

Shoko Miyabayashi was a Buddhist studies scholar who completed undergraduate and master's studies at Taisho University (1948–1955). He later taught there, serving as lecturer (1960), assistant professor (1962), and Dean of the Faculty of Buddhist Studies (1978–2002).

Shoko Miyata is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. As of 2026, Miyata is attested as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Shoko Takeuchi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University. Takeuchi later served at Ryukoku University, where an appointment as professor emeritus was attested between 1987 and 1995.

Shoko Watanabe was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Taisho University (1935–1943) and Toyo University (1956–1969), and an associate professorship at Kyushu University (1948–1953).

Shoku Bando is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Kyoto University of Education, Otani University, and the University of Freiburg. In 1987, he was affiliated with the Abhidharma Research Institute, Kyoto University, and Fukui Prefectural College.

Shoryu Katsura is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar who studied at Kyoto University and the University of Toronto under A. K. Warder. He held posts at Hiroshima University (1976–2004) and Ryukoku University (2004–2015).

Shoshin Fukihara was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University and Horyuji Kangakuin under Join Saeki and Susumu Yamaguchi. He served as professor at Otani University and Otani University Junior College, and assistant professor at Doho University.
Shoshin Higuchi is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer at Otani University (attested in 1998) and as a committee member of the Otani Society (attested in 2000).

Shoshin Kuwayama is a scholar of history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1957 to 1966 and served there as an assistant professor from circa 1966 to 2002.
